name: SK6812 RGBW LED strip (60 LEDs/m, 5 V)
description: Flexible strip of individually addressable SK6812RGBW LEDs (OPSCO 5050 package: red, green, blue and a white LED die plus a driver IC in each pixel), 60 per metre, chained on one 800 kbit/s data wire with 32 bits per LED (8 each of G, R, B, W). Runs on 5 V (datasheet 3.5-5.5 V absolute, characterised at 4.5-5.5 V); up to about 80 mA per LED with all four channels at full, 4.8 A per metre. Sold as: BTF-LIGHTING SK6812 RGBW LED strip, 60 LEDs/m, DC5V, 1 m (60 pixels), white PCB IP30, with a 3-pin JST-SM input lead to the +5V, DI, GND pads.
eli5: A bendy ribbon of 60 tiny lights that can each glow any colour or a proper white, all controlled through one data wire.

pins.name: +5V
pins.description: LED supply, 5 V regulated (4.5-5.5 V; above 5.5 V destroys the LEDs). Up to 4.8 A for 60 LEDs at full RGBW: feed it from a separate 5 V supply whose GND joins the board's GND.

pins.name: DI
pins.description: Data in to the first LED (follow the arrows printed on the strip). Datasheet VIH is 3.4 V at VDD 5 V, so 3.3 V GPIO is marginal: a 74AHCT125 level shifter is recommended, plus a 300-500 ohm series resistor.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the microcontroller and the 5 V supply (white wire on many BTF/JST-SM leads)

buildNotes: Wire the INPUT end: the arrows on the strip point away from it, and its pads read +5V, DI, GND. Data sent into the DO end does nothing.

Power +5V from a separate regulated 5 V supply sized for the strip (60 LEDs x 80 mA = 4.8 A at full RGBW; 6 A supply for a full metre) and join its GND to the board's GND. Never exceed 5.5 V (datasheet absolute maximum).
The driver's default brightness of 0.1 keeps a full-white metre near 0.5 A; each dark LED still draws about 1 mA (datasheet IDD).

Datasheet logic-high threshold VIH is 3.4 V minimum at VDD 5 V, above a 3.3 V GPIO's high level: use a 74AHCT125 (or similar 5 V-supplied HCT/AHCT buffer) on DI for reliable data. Put a 300-500 ohm resistor in series with DI and a 1000 uF capacitor across +5V and GND at the strip.
Each LED takes 32 bits in G, R, B, W order. Use neopixel.NeoPixel(pin, n, bpp=4) (or the driver) and give colours as (r, g, b, w); with bpp=3 the colours shift along the strip.
Bit timing (datasheet): T0H 0.3 us, T1H 0.6 us (+-0.15 us), bit period 1.25 us +-0.6 us; a low of at least 80 us latches the data.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from sk6812_rgbw import SK6812RGBW

strip = SK6812RGBW(Pin({DI}), 60, brightness=0.5)
strip.clear()
strip.show()
time.sleep(1)
strip.fill((0, 0, 0, 160))
strip.pixel(0, (200, 0, 0, 0))
strip.show()
print('white', strip.get(5), 'first', strip.get(0))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: The strip starts dark, then lights white with a red first LED and reports the bytes sent
